items.title: John Casimir Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: Yeah, but some of it you told me it was written out by a guy. Who would write it down? Oh, sure. Louis Dumaine.

ctx.x: I'm going to leave from the club to go to the church and the other store, the ground and the other store. Yeah. I'm going to leave there with a hammer, you see. Play more soil and hammer till I get there. Then I'm going to go ahead and get ready to lay the stone and play a funeral marches. And then after the stone was laid, do you stay at the church or do you go back to the club or what? Well, you'd be finished at the stone leading. I see. Then we'd be marching back in. Every red ring would be marching back to…

Now, how do you get your sheet music for the young tuxedo? How do you get your music for the young tuxedo? You told me you order that and then sometimes... I stand up and get my hand. Yeah, but some of it you told me it was written out by a guy. Who would write it down? Oh, sure. Louis Dumaine. Louis Dumaine, huh? Louis Dumaine, huh? You paid $4.39? Yeah. That's one.
That's one arrangement? Two. Two of them. The eternal last rest, the eternal peace. Mm-hmm.
